title: San Lorenzo, early Olmec capital
summary: San Lorenzo, in southern Veracruz, is described as the premier Early Formative Olmec capital. Occupied from about 1500 BCE, it peaked between 1200 and 850 BCE, with large earthen architecture and 129 stone monuments including ten colossal heads. La Venta later became the Olmec capital.

uncertainty.note: Encyclopedia.com (Cyphers) gives a peak of 1200–850 BCE; Minerva gives flowering from about 1400 to 1000 BC. The record uses the first.

as_recorded.value: occupation from about 1500 bce; peak between 1200 and 850 bce
flowering from about 1400 BC to 1000 BC

where.modern_name: San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán, southern Veracruz, Mexico

importance.justification: Encyclopedia.com calls it the premier Early Formative Olmec capital, the centre of the Olmec world for over three centuries.
